title: NC House Public Access Act of 2025
lastAction: Ref to the Com on Appropriations, if favorable, Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill appropriates $91,000 in nonrecurring funds and $4,000 in recurring annual funds to install and maintain equipment that allows the public to watch North Carolina House committee meetings and floor proceedings live online and access recordings for 10 years. Committee chairs may choose not to record meetings if they provide advance notice and maintain audio recordings and written minutes instead.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill increases government transparency and civic engagement by making legislative proceedings more accessible to busy North Carolinians who cannot attend in person. Providing online access and archival recordings allows citizens to better understand how their representatives vote on bills and hold them accountable, strengthening democratic participation across the state.
aiConArguments: Opponents may express concerns about the recurring costs to maintain the system over time and question whether the appropriated funds represent the most efficient use of limited state resources. Some may also worry that allowing committee chairs to opt out of video recording creates inconsistency in transparency, or that certain discussions might be chilled if participants know they are being recorded and broadcast online.
